name: Europa
role: Phoenician princess carried to Crete by Zeus in the form of a bull
fun_fact: Her name was eventually given to the continent of Europe, though Greek writers first used it for the mainland north of Crete.

name: Minos
role: Legendary king of Crete and of the palace at Knossos
fun_fact: Homer already imagines Minos as a judge of the dead, holding a golden sceptre in the underworld.

name: Pasiphae
role: Queen of Crete, wife of Minos and mother of the Minotaur
fun_fact: Her name means 'all-shining', and in some genealogies she is a daughter of the sun god Helios and a sister of Circe.

name: Minotaur
role: Bull-headed monster kept in the labyrinth at Knossos
fun_fact: The creature's birth name was Asterius, which is also the name of the Cretan king who adopted Minos.

name: Daedalus
role: Legendary Athenian craftsman and builder of the labyrinth
fun_fact: Greek writers said his statues were so lifelike that they had to be tied down to stop them walking away.

name: Icarus
role: Son of Daedalus who flew too near the sun and fell
fun_fact: The sea where he fell was named the Icarian after him, and the island beside it was called Icaria.

name: Theseus
role: Athenian hero who entered the labyrinth and killed the Minotaur
fun_fact: Athenian tradition also credited Theseus with uniting the villages of Attica into one city, an act called synoikismos.

name: Ariadne
role: Cretan princess who gave Theseus the thread and helped him escape
fun_fact: Some scholars connect her name with a Mycenaean Greek tablet from Knossos that addresses a 'Lady of the Labyrinth'.

name: Atreus
role: Mycenaean king whose feud with his brother cursed his descendants
fun_fact: The great round tomb at Mycenae is called the Treasury of Atreus by visitors, a name given by later travellers rather than by any ancient inscription.

name: Agamemnon
role: King of Mycenae and leader of the Greek expedition against Troy
fun_fact: The gold mask found at Mycenae in 1876 is still displayed as the 'Mask of Agamemnon', although it is centuries older than any Trojan War.
